tools.name: shaniu_stats
tools.description: Live SHANIU stats: total supply, claim pool remaining, claim count, current claim fee (wei of BNB, ~0.2 USD via Chainlink oracle), whether claiming is open, and optionally a wallet's balance / claimed status.

tools.name: shaniu_prepare_claim
tools.description: Prepare an unsigned claim() (mint) transaction. Caller wallet must hold a Binance Agent ID (.ai); one claim per address; reward is a block-hash lottery (50-150 typical, up to 21,000; last claim sweeps the pool). Returns {to, data, valueWei} to sign with the user's wallet.

tools.name: shaniu_market_orders
tools.description: List currently fillable sell orders on the on-chain order book, cheapest first. Each order: id, maker, remainingSHANIU, priceBNBperToken. No AMM pool exists — buying fills these orders atomically.

tools.name: shaniu_prepare_buy
tools.description: Prepare an unsigned buy transaction that fills one or more sell orders. Computes exact BNB cost. Single order uses the market contract; multiple orders use the cart contract (buyMany) in one tx.

tools.name: shaniu_prepare_list
tools.description: Prepare unsigned transactions to list SHANIU for sale: (1) approve the market contract, (2) list(amount, priceWei). The tokens stay in the seller's wallet until filled — the market is authorization-based, no custody.

tools.name: shaniu_invite_stats
tools.description: Referral program stats: global slots/budget usage, and (with address) one inviter's bound count, earned and pending SHANIU. Invite link format: https://bn.shaniu.ai/?ref=<address>

tools.name: shaniu_invite_register
tools.description: Register a referral binding. Prefer mode=intent BEFORE the invitee calls claim(); or bind after the fact with the invitee's claim tx hash. Always ask your user for consent first. Rewards (10/50/200/1000 SHANIU tiers) roll automatically and are paid in batches.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "shaniu_prepare_list" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
